prompt: Implement ONLY Phase 1A of the approved BrandBox AI admin architecture plan in the project worktree. You may edit project files, but keep scope strictly to database role expansion and RBAC foundation; do not build the users UI, roles UI, AI costs, billing, queue, or unrelated admin modules. Requirements: (1) add a new Supabase migration with a valid timestamped filename later than existing migrations that safely expands public.app_role with PLATFORM_ADMIN, OPERATIONS_MANAGER, CONTENT_MANAGER, USER_MANAGER, SUPPORT_AGENT, FINANCE_MANAGER, MARKETING_MANAGER, SECURITY_AUDITOR, ANALYST, preserving existing USER, SUPPORT, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN values and all existing rows; do NOT add OWNER to the normal app_role enum because OWNER is a protected platform concept and must not become dropdown-assignable; (2) refactor src/lib/auth/rbac-engine.ts into the canonical RBAC source with modern resource.action permissions, Arabic/English role labels/descriptions, role risk/access metadata, fixed permission sets for all roles, and a compatibility mapping so existing legacy uppercase permission calls continue to work during transition; (3) preserve current behavior for legacy ADMIN and SUPPORT through explicit compatibility/alias permission sets rather than silently rewriting database rows; (4) add helpers needed by later API/UI phases to query role definitions, assignability, descriptions, and permissions, but do not expose secrets; (5) enforce in RBAC metadata that SUPER_ADMIN is the highest assignable administrative role and USER is non-admin; OWNER must remain outside ordinary assignment; (6) update only directly necessary TypeScript role types/imports that would otherwise fail build because of the expanded canonical role definitions; avoid broad refactors; (7) add focused tests for the RBAC matrix/legacy compatibility if an appropriate existing test structure exists, without weakening existing tests. Security invariants: default deny, no permission wildcard for ordinary roles, SECURITY_AUDITOR and ANALYST are read-only, SUPPORT_AGENT is limited, no provider secret/API-key permission except the highest trusted operational/admin roles, and role metadata must clearly state what each role can and cannot do. Before finishing, run only the existing relevant focused tests/build checks that are possible without changing environment configuration. Do not run git commit/push. Return a concise report listing changed files, migration details, permission model, compatibility behavior, tests/build results, and any blockers for Phase 1B.
